## [0.0.8] - 2026-11-23

### Fixed

- HTML charts remain offline files. The plugin no longer tries to register an experimental host artifact provider on each render; this did not publish a shareable URL on supported hosts.

### Changed

- The tools RPC transport is source-contract's `tools-rpc` module, pinned at
  `github:we-the-rebel-alliance/source-contract#v0.3.0` and bundled into `dist/index.js`. The vendored copy of the module
  and its `check-copies` entry are gone; the method table, each method's class and its permission action, and every
  refusal are unchanged, so a script sees the same methods and the same answers. Its MIT licence is listed in
  `THIRD_PARTY_NOTICES.md` and shipped in `licenses/packages/`.
- CI: a run by hand no longer shares a concurrency group with a push on the same ref.
- No host-support change: still tested on 2.2.3, 2.2.4, 2.2.5, 2.2.6, 2.2.7, 2.3.0, 2.3.1 and 2.3.2, with the supported range
  unchanged (`>=2.2.3 <2.4.0`).

### Known limits

- **No PDF output, and no Plotly input.** Mermaid is supported for the five diagram kinds in `charts_diagram`; other Mermaid kinds (`gantt`, `pie`, `journey`, `gitGraph`) are refused with the kinds that work. [docs/status.md](https://github.com/joe-broadhead/opencode-charts/blob/HEAD/docs/status.md) says what does not work and why, and `charts_capabilities` reports what this build supports.
- **Bundled fonts cover Latin, Greek and Cyrillic.** A label beyond them gets `FONT_GLYPH_MISSING`; the fix is a font file with `theme.font.files`.
- **Built-in themes cover neutral, product and editorial palettes.** The nine include the neutral `light`, `dark`, `high-contrast`, `print` and `presentation`, the Geist pair, and the FT and Economist palettes. A brand theme is saved per workspace with `charts_theme_save`, set in the plugin's options, or derived from a host `seed`.
- **Nothing is loaded from the network.** A remote data file or image is not fetched.
- **Diagrams have a size limit.** A Mermaid diagram (a `dsl`, or an `architecture` recipe) may have 150 nodes and 200 edges; a larger one is refused with `SPEC_TOO_EXPENSIVE` before any layout, because the layout grows much faster than the input. Within the limits a layout takes up to about 7 s and 370 MB, always inside the default 10 s deadline. The Unicode outline is drawn up to 40 nodes and 60 edges and within 2 s; past that it is the title line.
- **Recipes cover the 14 standard types.** The other 65 catalogue entries are not recipes: 56 are raw engine specs, 2 are tables for `charts_table` and 7 are diagrams for `charts_diagram`. An engine document keeps its native layout (no outer-size fitting or responsive reflow) and its own interaction syntax.
- **Four interaction presets.** Tooltip, legend highlight, temporal x zoom and scatter/bubble brush, in the documented
  combinations; no series hiding, no ECharts zoom or brush, and SVG/PNG always show the initial view.
- **PNG and HTML need the packaged runtime.** A missing runtime is reported as `PNG_UNAVAILABLE` or `HTML_UNAVAILABLE`; reinstalling the plugin restores it.
- **Some catalogue examples have rough edges.** Close-set ticks in the histogram and binned heatmap examples.
- **Package size.** The package is about 14.5 MB unpacked: the plugin is about 5.3 MB (`dist/index.js`, which every engine start loads, is about 170 KB; the renderer it loads on the first call is the rest) and the render worker `dist/vega-worker.js` about 2.8 MB (it carries Vega and, since 0.0.5, the diagram engine): Vega, Vega-Lite, ECharts, Observable Plot, the diagram and table engines, and the PNG rasteriser are bundled, so a render needs no network.
- **Host range.** OpenCode `>=2.2.3 <2.4.0`, tested on 2.2.3, 2.2.4, 2.2.5, 2.2.6, 2.2.7, 2.3.0, 2.3.1 and 2.3.2.

## [0.0.6] - 2026-11-15

### Changed

- **An engine start no longer loads the chart engines.** The plugin is split: `dist/index.js`, which every engine start
  evaluates, holds the tool table, options, status and RPCs, with no zod schema and no engine; Vega, Vega-Lite,
  ECharts, Observable Plot, resvg's loader, the diagram layout, the table and dashboard builders and the tools' zod
  schemas are in `dist/renderer.js` and `dist/chunks/`, loaded on the first tool call, the first script call or the
  first input check, once. Measured inside a real engine start with only Charts loaded (the plugin's import plus its
  setup, median of 5, on a shared Linux VM): **726 ms → 19 ms on stock OpenCode 2.3.0, and 714 ms → 17 ms on 2.2.6**.
  The first call pays the load instead: a first `validate` went from 513 ms to 1,150 ms on 2.3.0 (537 ms to 1,194 ms
  on 2.2.6), so a start and its first chart take about as long as before, and a start that draws nothing saves it
  all. A render's deadline starts after the load, so no call gets less time to render.
- **The tools are registered from a table the build computes** from the registry (`src/tool-table.ts`): the same names,
  descriptions, output schemas and input JSON Schemas, which are zod's own. Each tool's input is a Standard Schema that
  validates with the tool's zod schema, so OpenCode reports the same issues and passes the same parsed input. The theme
  RPC loads its theme code on the first `sync`, and `/charts-status` loads the theme store when it runs.
- CI reads the stock OpenCode releases it installs from `TESTED_HOSTS` (`scripts/tested-hosts.mjs`), as the release
  workflow does, instead of a list of its own.

### Known limits

- **No PDF output, and no Plotly input.** Mermaid is supported for the five diagram kinds in `charts_diagram`; other Mermaid kinds (`gantt`, `pie`, `journey`, `gitGraph`) are refused with the kinds that work.   combinations; no series hiding, no ECharts zoom or brush, and SVG/PNG always show the initial view.

## [0.0.5] - 2026-11-15

### Added

- **OpenCode 2.3.** The host range is `>=2.2.3 <2.4.0`, tested on 2.2.3, 2.2.4, 2.2.5, 2.2.6, 2.2.7 and 2.3.0, and CI
  runs the host suite on every one of them. Nothing in the plugin depends on what 2.3.0 changes: it starts no
  subagent, reads no `session.tool.failed` event and registers no `session.fork` hook. A tool call still runs to its
  render deadline after Stop, as it did on 2.2.

### Fixed

- **A diagram can no longer exhaust the host's memory.** A Mermaid diagram (a `dsl`, or an `architecture` recipe) is
  refused before any layout past 150 nodes or 200 edges, with `SPEC_TOO_EXPENSIVE` naming the limit; Mermaid's layout
  grows much faster than its input, and within the 20,000-character `dsl` limit a 600-edge flowchart took 15 s and
  6.8 GB, and 1,500 edges more than 150 s. Within the limits a layout takes up to about 7 s and 370 MB (15 nested
  subgraphs at 150 nodes and 200 edges), always inside the default 10 s deadline.
  `charts_validate` takes the same path.
- **Diagrams lay out in the render worker,** under the same wall-clock limit (`CHARTS_RENDER_TIMEOUT_MS`) and 256 MB
  heap cap as Vega, so a layout that runs away is stopped and the OpenCode process never blocks. The Unicode outline is
  a second job with its own 2 s deadline, drawn only up to 40 nodes and 60 edges: Mermaid's outline router can loop
  without end on some three-line inputs, and an outline stopped at its deadline is left out with a warning while the
  drawing stands. With `CHARTS_IN_PROCESS=1` a Mermaid diagram returns no outline.
- **User colours are checked as colours.** A table's `badgeColors` and a diagram node's `color` take `#hex`, `rgb()`,
  `rgba()`, `transparent`, a CSS colour name or a `theme:` token, and nothing else; a value such as
  `red" style="cursor:url(…)` is refused with its JSON path. Colour arithmetic never passes on a value that is not a
  colour, and every colour the table and diagram engines write into an attribute is escaped.
- **The SVG check refuses external CSS references.** `checkRenderedSvg` refuses a `url()` to anything but an internal
  `#id`, `@import` and `image()`, in presentation attributes, `style` attributes and `<style>` elements, with CSS escapes
  and XML entities decoded first.
- **THIRD_PARTY_NOTICES.md names elkjs's source** (EPL-2.0): github.com/kieler/elkjs at the bundled tag, as it does for
  resvg.

### Changed

- `charts_update`'s `appearance.hash` is a hash of the tokens drawn, and a layout profile sets the typography, so a
  `layout` patch changes the hash (as it has since 0.0.4); `appearance.theme` and `appearance.base` say whether the
  theme itself changed. docs/documents.md says so.
